objective: Test a bounded plateau model by separating small-task overhead, batch filling, physical-layout response, and dynamic GPU admission. Do not estimate or recommend a point optimum.

secondary_objectives: scan task span as a fraction of query elapsed time
GPU semaphore-holding share of scan span
task count and batches per task
decoded rows and bytes per task
task footprint, retry, split-retry, and spill
contract.descriptive_plateau: candidate median no more than 5% slower than the best observed median
contract.safety: no retry, split-retry, spill, executor loss, or result mismatch

queries.variable_width: same numeric columns plus payment_type string

layouts.sharded: 825 small one-row-group files across the full corpus
layouts.source: original monthly files with one large row group per file

testbed.codec: Snappy only; codec contrast remains future work

analysis.variance: Report all ten default values, CV, and a planning MDE. Do not reuse the planning estimate as confirmatory evidence.
mechanisms: Fit effective incremental task cost against actual scan-task count on the small side.
Measure batch filling separately at fixed partition size.
Use gpuMaxConcurrentGpuTasks and semaphore wait to test whether c(P) changes.
Treat maxPartitionBytes as an input to Spark packing, not realized task bytes.
Treat no observed retry/spill as a censored upper wall, not proof of safety.
analysis.layout: Compare whether changing maxPartitionBytes changes actual scan task count and elapsed time in each physical layout.
analysis.validation: The follow-up is exploratory mechanism evidence. A later held-out run must validate any plateau rule.

pre_registered_invariants: All result hashes are stable within query/layout.
The 128-MiB setting produces at least as many scan tasks as every larger treatment in the sharded layout.
Changing batch target at fixed partition layout changes emitted batch size before it is interpreted as a performance mechanism.
Dynamic concurrency values are treated as ranges/invariants, never exact reproducibility targets.
If no retry/spill/split event occurs, the memory cliff remains unobserved.
limitations: Warm filesystem cache is not reset.
Source and sharded layouts preserve rows but not production file locality.
The experiment does not intentionally force an OOM beyond the natural sweep.
